excerpt: A small open-source take on the "AI teacher that draws on a whiteboard" idea: a model writes a lesson as strict JSON, code validates it, and a browser player draws it in time with the narration. Everything here (prompts, schema, player) is original code. Live demo: a lesson written by DeepSeek, played by the single-file player (press Play, untick "Silent" for voice). topic --> planner.py --(LLM)--> lesson.json --> validator.js --(issues)--> repair loop | v player.html (SVG draw-on + speech, cues by word index) open player.html # plays the built-in rainbow sample (no server needed) node validator.js samples/rainbow.json # exit 0 = valid; prints issues as JSON otherwise export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=... # default provider; stdlib only, no pip install needed python3 planner.py --topic "How tides work" --minutes 4 --out lesson.json \ --price-in <USD per 1M input tokens> --price-out <USD per 1M output tokens> --inr-per-usd 88 # then open player.html, "Load a lesson", pick lesson.json # or: python3 -m http.server and open player.html?src=lesson.json&autoplay=1 # Anthropic instead: pip install anthropic; export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...; add --provider anthropic --model (or env LESSON_MODEL) picks the model; the default is deepseek-flash. Prices are inputs on purpose: the planner prints tokens and cost per lesson so you can measure your real number. --topic - reads the topic from stdin; --research-file adds reference notes; --dry-run prints the prompts. beats[] each hold narration plus ops[]: heading, paragraph, callout, definition, table, figure. A figure is parts[] of marks[] (circle, ellipse, rect, line, path, label). Each part has a cue: the index of the narration word at which it is drawn. Paths use absolute commands only. checks[] are end-of-lesson multiple-choice questions. python3 -m unittest test_planner # repair loop, parsing, cost math (fake LLM, no key needed) python3 test_player.py # headless Chrome: playback, quiz, bad input, XSS safety python3 build.py # regenerate…
